name: CA-43
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+27 district partisanship makes the seat structurally safe for Democrats
Waters holds a roughly 75-to-1 cash-on-hand advantage over the challenger
Long-serving incumbent faces an essentially unfunded opponent
No public polls or expert ratings; markets price about 97% Democratic
model.rationale: The district's D+27 lean, Waters' incumbency, and a lopsided financial picture—about $330,000 on hand versus a few hundred dollars for Morales—leave no plausible path for an upset, and prediction markets agree at roughly 97% Democratic.
model.watch: A late-breaking scandal, health event, or sudden outside-spending infusion for the challenger would be the only realistic threat to the expected outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 43rd District is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 27 points toward Democrats. Maxine Waters, a longtime incumbent, advanced to the general election and faces Republican Cristian Morales, who has run a minimal campaign. Waters has raised about $1 million and holds more than $330,000 on hand, while Morales reported under $14,000 raised and only a few hundred dollars in the bank. No outside groups have invested meaningfully in the race.

No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have flagged the contest as competitive. Prediction markets price Waters near 97% to win. The combination of the district's heavy Democratic lean, Waters' incumbency and financial dominance, and the challenger's lack of resources makes an upset highly unlikely, though the absence of polling leaves some uncertainty about the exact margin.
